learning_outcomes.description: Source, construct and disseminate a piece of investigative journalism.
Formulate, compose and assess advanced investigative measures such as Freedom of Information or Right To Information requests.
Critically analyse the diverse needs of audiences in the interests of working towards a more fair, just, inclusive and equitable society.
Embed the traditions, theories, frameworks and codes of ethics in reporting practice with moral courage in decison making.
Apply a wide range of journalistic research methods, including data-driven reporting, social media investigation, interviewing, observation and document-driven reporting.
Critically assess, interpret and apply use of technological developments including AI to search and organise information.

assessments.task_description:
Throughout the semester, essential practical skills are assigned and submitted in tutorials as a complete portfolio. Students should refer to Blackboard for the portfolio platform. Elements will be released weekly but include: using AI for investigative research and interrogation, digital verification, document discovery, interview and research plans.

The portfolio skillset that this portfolio will assess is completed and uploaded in tutorials only so regular attendance and participation is crucial. Your 5 best tasks out of the 8 will form the made. These tasks are designed to support the final assessment task (Major News Investigation). As part of the portfolio students must gain approval (see Blackboard for details) from their tutor in week 9 for their Major News Investigation.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Notebook/ Logbook, Portfolio
assessments.task_description:
This portfolio will require you to submit a substantive piece of investigative journalism. 

This assessment task requires you to go out and produce a substantive piece of investigative journalism. The portfolio must include four elements:

  1. Progress diary/journal and sources list (template provided on Blackboard).
  2. A piece of written investigative journalism in either news or feature style.
  3. At least one visual or multimedia element, which could include a data visualisation, chart, map, photograph(s), audio, video or another approved visual or multimedia element. The visual elements should enhance and value-add to the investigative story you have produced, and more than one type of visual or multimedia element may be used. 
  4. AI Coversheet (template provided on Blackboard, this will include ethical and transparency considerations).

The investigative story should include a minimum of four primary sources (more is encouraged) and be 800-1000 words. Your tutor needs to approve your investigation by week 9 to manage any possible risks to yourself, or to the public, or to the environment. In instances where the multimedia components of the submission are substantial (e.g. long-form audio or video, photographic essay), a reduction in the word count of the associated story may be approved by your tutor, but this must be negotiated prior to the end of Week 9. 

Your investigation should be presented digitally, using Shorthand or another approved platform. The text elements of your investigation must also be submitted via TurnItIn, alongside a sources page and research diary/journal (templates available on Blackboard). You will be expected to record your sources and diary as you go so that we can verify the information in your final story.

In this course your tutors are prepared to read drafts for the Major News Investigation. However, several conditions apply:

  1. Only one draft will be read per student.
  2. Drafts for the Major News Investigation assessment must be submitted in class or at a drop-in session in or prior to Week 12. Any drafts received after this time will not be read.
  3. Draft reading is embedded in this course to replicate a newsroom environment and as a learning tool to help you develop journalistic writing.
  4. Drafts will not be considered over email.

Detailed assessment criteria will be provided via Blackboard.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Your investigation should be presented digitally, using Shorthand or another approved platform. The text elements of your investigation must also be submitted via TurnItIn, alongside a sources page and research journal (templates available on Blackboard). Include a link to the digital publication in your TurnItIn submission.
